question: If the length of a conductor is doubled, then the resistance of the conductor will be: (other parameters are kept same)
solution:
The correct answer is __**doubled**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Resistance (R) of a conductor is directly proportional to its length (L).
 
• When the length of the conductor is doubled, the resistance also doubles.
 
• This relationship is described by the formula R = ρ(L/A), where ρ is the resistivity and A is the cross-sectional area.
 
• Resistivity (ρ) and the cross-sectional area (A) remain constant in this scenario.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:** This law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points and inversely proportional to the resistance.
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:** Besides length, resistance is affected by the material's resistivity, cross-sectional area, and temperature.
 
• **Resistivity (ρ):** A material-specific property that quantifies how strongly a given material opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• **Applications:** Understanding resistance changes with length is crucial in designing electrical circuits, wires, and components.
 
• **Practical Implications:** In practical applications, long conductors are usually designed with larger cross-sectional areas to minimize resistance and power loss.
